clue.text: Old boy in a haunt designed in the German way

indicators.note: the old boy is placed inside the reworked letters, sitting within them
something designed has been drawn up afresh, so these letters are laid out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged
OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil designs a haunt in German style.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'in' appears twice: the first places OB inside, the second just joins wordplay to definition. Bahn is German for road or way.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, literally a 'car road', so it is a highway of Germany.

clue.text: Imposing fellow in a posh sort of shirt

indicators.note: the fellow sits inside the remaining letters, enclosed by them

parts.note: taken as written
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
Gus is a man's name, any fellow
a T-shirt is a sort of shirt

explanation.surface: An imposing man wearing a smart kind of shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A, U and T make the outer shell, with GUS slotted between U and T to give A-U-GUS-T.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means majestic and dignified, inspiring reverence and respect.

clue.text: Garment provided for stingy son

definitions.note: tights is a plural noun used for a single garment

parts.note: tight is informal for mean with money
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone buys clothing for a son they are mean to.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a close-fitting item of clothing covering the legs and lower body.

clue.text: Where musicians are forbidden, say, to be candidates?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word for forbidden and write down a word with that sound

parts.note: a word meaning forbidden, spelt differently
to stand is to be a candidate in an election

explanation.surface: A wry question about musicians who are banned from running for office.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading; the whole clue also hints at the stand where a banned band might gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandstand is a covered outdoor platform in a park on which a brass band or other group performs.

clue.text: We probably give them a shock when we take their chairs

definitions.text: We probably give them a shock when we take their chairs

parts.words: We probably give them a shock when we take their chairs
parts.note: surface reading: people startled when we steal their seats
setter's reading: a shock is a mass of hair, which we bring to the salon when we sit in the stylist's seat

explanation.walkthrough: Shock sounds like a fright, but a shock of hair is a thick untidy mop; customers sit in their chairs and present them with one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressers cut and style hair, with clients seated in their salon chairs.

clue.text: Greek character is first to reach a popular resort

indicators.note: first says the word is goes at the front, ahead of the letter

parts.note: taken as written
chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written; it belongs to the wordplay as well

explanation.surface: A Greek person is the first to arrive at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty, ending the wordplay and starting the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples, well known as a holiday destination with spas.

clue.text: Remove impurities from the undergrowth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to clean by rubbing hard
second meaning: low stunted trees and bushes

explanation.surface: Clearing contamination out of the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to clean vigorously, and scrub is also land covered with stunted shrubs and brushwood.

clue.text: Punch provided for one working profitably in the sunshine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a heavy swinging blow

definitions.text: one working profitably in the sunshine
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who makes hay while the sun shines

explanation.surface: A drink served to a farm worker out in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch looks like a drink for the labourer; it is a blow. The second half echoes the saying 'make hay while the sun shines'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a wild swinging blow in boxing, and literally a person who cuts and dries grass for hay.

clue.text: The heartless deacon's terrible story

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle of the word goes, keeping its outer letters
terrible suggests the letters are in a dreadful state and need sorting

parts.note: the word with its middle letter dropped
taken as written, the possessive dropped

explanation.surface: A churchman tells a dreadful tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting account of a real incident, a kind of tale.

clue.text: Very large carriage required by old clown

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
antic was once a noun for a grotesque performer or buffoon

explanation.surface: A huge coach is needed by an elderly circus clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigantic means enormous, of a size like a giant's.

clue.text: Seaside wall on grey rocks

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, unsettling the order of these letters

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea wall built on grey stones.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocks reads as a noun the wall stands on, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low barrier built out from a beach to check erosion and drifting sand.

clue.text: Bi-national link-up a Spanish dictator found relevant once

parts.note: General Franco ruled Spain from 1939 to 1975
germane means relevant; german is its old spelling

explanation.surface: A Spanish strongman judges a two-country alliance pertinent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the archaic sense: german was an old form of germane, meaning pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Franco-German agreement or partnership involves France and Germany together, two nations allied.

clue.text: Locates spectacles, say

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word for spectacles and write a word with that sound

parts.note: sights are spectacles, things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Someone finds their glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: Spectacles suggests glasses; here it means sights, as in sights of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to place or position it, so sites works as a verb for situates.

clue.text: A target for river administrators

parts.note: the Dart is a river in Devon, in south-west England
a board is a body of people who manage an organisation

explanation.surface: A goal set for the managers of a river authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the circular target that darts are thrown at in the pub game.

clue.text: Manufacture suitable objects primarily to scrape a living

indicators.note: primarily says the word for objects comes before the word for suitable, reversing their clue order

parts.note: to make is to manufacture
ends are aims or objectives
meet is an old word for fitting or proper

explanation.surface: Producing the right goods first is the way to earn enough to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Objects means purposes, not things; meet as an adjective is archaic for proper.
explanation.definitionFit: To make ends meet is the idiom for having just enough money to cover one's expenses.

clue.text: E.g. crabby type — and inconsiderate, it's said in the pub

indicators.note: speech in the pub is slurred by drink, so we hear the word as a tipsy person pronounces it

parts.note: selfish, slurred with a drunken sh sound

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered, thoughtless person holding forth at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Crabby looks like grumpy, but it means crab-like; a drinker's lisp turns selfish into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crab is an example of a shellfish, an aquatic animal with a protective shell.

clue.text: Jittery person watching birds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who twitches nervously

definitions.note: the clue gives an activity; the answer is the person doing it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an obsessive birdwatcher chasing rare sightings

explanation.surface: A nervous person out birdwatching.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is slang for a keen birder who travels to spot rarities, as well as one who fidgets.

clue.text: Tangled hair of the Spanish sheep, say

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
sheep gather in flocks

explanation.surface: The matted wool of Spanish sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Elf-locks are matted knots of hair, once blamed on mischievous elves tangling it at night.

clue.text: Kindly writer, embracing girl, sat for portrait

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the writer wraps around the girl

parts.note: H.G. Wells, the English novelist
Di is short for Diana, a girl's name
a sitter poses for a painter

explanation.surface: A generous author hugs a young woman while posing for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindly looks like an adverb describing the writer, but it is the adjective being defined. H.G. Wells wrote The War of the Worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-disposed means friendly and favourably inclined towards someone, as kindly does.

clue.text: Account to cover day on a safari here

indicators.note: to cover is to go over something, so the account wraps around the day

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation for account
Fri is short for Friday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A report covering a day spent on safari.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is the continent most associated with safaris, viewing wildlife in the savanna.

clue.text: Trains French eleven to win medal

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK railway operator
onze is French for eleven

explanation.surface: A French football side trains hard to take a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleven suggests a football team, but it is just the French number.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze is the third-place medal in a competition, so it stands for the award by its metal.

clue.text: American poplar newly lit up by an actor

indicators.note: newly means made in a fresh way, so these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: these letters rearranged
Sir Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a celebrated actor-manager

explanation.surface: A tree in America freshly lit up by a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip tree of North America is also known as the tulip poplar, after its flowers and leaves.

clue.text: Rice dish for the italian in the Pyrenean tourist centre

indicators.note: in places the Italian word inside the name of the town

parts.note: Pau is a French town at the foot of the Pyrenees
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian ordering a rice meal in a mountain resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, often with meat or vegetables added.

clue.text: Prisoner's poem written in middle of alert

indicators.note: written in means set down inside, so the poem goes within the other letters
middle of keeps only the central letters of the word after it

parts.note: the inner three letters of the word
If is a famous poem by Rudyard Kipling

explanation.surface: An inmate's verse composed in a state of watchfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay rather than making it possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifer is slang for someone serving a life sentence in jail.

clue.text: My goodness. Lebanese extremists barrack the speaker!

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: extremists are the ones at the ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Shock as Lebanese hardliners shout down an orator.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack is British for jeering at a speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a public speaker with taunts and jeers.

clue.text: Aspiration, it appears, in a doctor no one rejected

parts.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so these words are read backwards
the word it appears inside the rest, set within it

parts.note: no as written, and one as the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ambition seems to be lacking in a doctor nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It appears' looks like a parenthetical aside, but it is the instruction placing IT inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiration and ambition are synonyms: a strong desire to achieve something.

clue.text: Soldiers given second signal to deliver

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
S is the abbreviation for second
a cue is a signal to act or speak

explanation.surface: Troops get a second order to make their delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: Deliver here means set free, not hand over goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to save or free them, which is what rescue means.

clue.text: Undeveloped island with grass by end of lake

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island
the oat is a cereal grass

indicators.note: end of keeps just the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An unspoilt island of grassland beside a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch, from Gaelic, appears in Scottish place names such as Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not yet fully formed or developed.
